sum: - UBS cut its price target on PPLI from $56 to $45 and maintained a neutral rating; the new target implies 9.73% upside from the prior close.
- Analyst sentiment remains broadly positive: nine analysts rate the stock Buy, five Hold and one Sell, with a consensus rating of Moderate Buy and an average target of $53.08.
- PPLI reported a quarterly loss of $9.15 per share, far below the expected loss of $0.23, while revenue fell 3.6% year over year.
- Five stocks we like better than People Incorporated Common Stock.

People Incorporated Common Stock (NASDAQ:PPLI - Get Free Report) had its target price dropped by equities researchers at UBS Group from $56.00 to $45.00 in a research note issued to investors on Thursday, Benzinga reports. The firm currently has a "neutral" rating on the stock. UBS Group's price objective suggests a potential upside of 9.73% from the company's previous close.

Several other research firms have also recently weighed in on PPLI. TD Cowen decreased their price target on shares of People Incorporated Common Stock from $70.00 to $60.00 and set a "buy" rating on the stock in a report on Wednesday. Zacks Research lowered People Incorporated Common Stock from a "strong-buy" rating to a "hold" rating in a research note on Monday, October 5th. Citigroup reduced their target price on People Incorporated Common Stock from $52.00 to $47.00 and set a "buy" rating for the company in a research report on Wednesday. JPMorgan Chase & Co. assumed coverage on People Incorporated Common Stock in a research note on Friday, September 11th. They issued an "overweight" rating and a $54.00 target price on the stock. Finally, Truist Financial lowered their price target on People Incorporated Common Stock from $62.00 to $59.00 and set a "buy" rating on the stock in a report on Wednesday. Nine research analysts have rated the stock with a Buy rating, five have given a Hold rating and one has assigned a Sell rating to the company's stock. Based on data from MarketBeat, the company presently has an average rating of "Moderate Buy" and a consensus target price of $53.08.
Shares of PPLI stock traded down $0.98 during trading hours on Thursday, reaching $41.01. The stock had a trading volume of 1,641,168 shares, compared to its average volume of 1,112,855.

sum: UBS raised its target on Lenskart to Rs 850 from Rs 800 earlier, calling it one of the most compelling compounding stories in India's consumer sector.

Lenskart Solutions Ltd shares rallied 11 per cent in Thursday's trade amid sharp upward revisions in target prices by a handful of domestic and foreign brokerages. These included UBS, which raised its target on Lenskart to Rs 850 from Rs 800 earlier, calling it one of the most compelling compounding stories in India's consumer sector. Morgan Stanley raised its target to Rs 805 from Rs 718.

ICICI Securities now values the stock at Rs 800, up from Rs 700 earlier. Goldman Sachs raised its target to Rs 800 from Rs 715, Emkay to Rs 800 from Rs 775, CLSA to Rs 773 from Rs 743 and Antique Stock Broking to Rs 660 from Rs 600.
On Wednesday, the scrip rose 11.05 per cent to hit a high of Rs 767.40 apiece.

Analysts said Lenskart has built strong moats in a difficult-to-scale category through a centralised, automated manufacturing facility and logistics network, strong backward integration and a large omnichannel presence.

HSBC upgraded the stock to 'Buy' and raised its target price to Rs 790 on higher estimates and a higher valuation multiple for its international business. Following the Q2 results, the foreign brokerage said its key upgrades were in India Ebitda margins, where the pace of expansion was higher, leading to an 8 per cent increase in its FY28 Ebitda estimates. For the international business, HSBC assumed higher growth and greater margin improvement.

"Our store expansion is higher than management estimates as we expect a pick-up. This drives a 17 per cent increase in international FY28e EBITDA. We roll forward our valuation to December 2027 and increase the international business target EV/EBITDA to 40x, from 30x, reflecting greater confidence in its growth and margin, while retaining 45x for India," it said.

The stock was trading at Rs 390.80, up Rs 10.70, or 2.82 per cent, on the NSE at 10:51 am. At the current market price (CMP), BEL shares have an upside potential of around 25 per cent to UBS' target price of Rs 500, while Jefferies sees a potential upside of nearly 25 per cent to its target price of Rs 490.
Motilal Oswal has a higher target price of Rs 540, implying an upside of around 38 per cent from the current market price. The brokerage has reiterated its Buy rating on the stock.
The stock has a 52-week high of Rs 473.45, recorded on March 6, 2026, and a 52-week low of Rs 354.55, touched on October 23, 2026. BEL's total market capitalisation stood at Rs 2,85,702.71 crore.

Navratna defence public sector undertaking Bharat Electronics Ltd on Friday reported a 19.8 per cent YoY rise in consolidated revenue from operations to Rs 7,291 crore in the September quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 5,764 crore in the corresponding period of the previous financial year.

The company's profit after tax (PAT) rose 19.8 per cent to Rs 1,541 crore in Q2 FY27, against Rs 1,286 crore in the year-ago period. Profit before tax (PBT) increased 19 per cent to Rs 2,064 crore in the September quarter, compared with Rs 1,734 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
For the first half of FY27, revenue from operations increased 26 per cent to Rs 12,824 crore from Rs 10,180 crore in the corresponding period of the previous year.

Dangote Cement stock: Goldman, UBS join London listing plans
sum: Dangote Cement stock is gaining attention after Goldman Sachs and UBS joined preparations for a possible London Stock Exchange listing. BusinessDay reported on October 15, 2026 that the company could pursue the transaction as early as November, with a proposed secondary sale targeting up to 1 billion US dollars.

The reported transaction would involve existing shareholders selling part of their holdings rather than Dangote Cement issuing new shares. Goldman Sachs and UBS would join other banks working on the proposed offering, which is intended to give the company access to a broader international investor base.

The London plan would complement Dangote Cement's existing listing on the Nigerian Exchange. For investors, a second listing could create an additional venue for trading and establish a reference point for the company's valuation among international institutions. The proposal does not by itself confirm that a transaction will be completed.

BusinessDay said the listing could take place as early as November. The timetable remains dependent on regulatory approvals, final terms and market conditions, while the reported sale structure would direct proceeds to selling shareholders rather than directly to Dangote Cement.

Investors should therefore distinguish between progress in arranging the transaction and a completed London debut. The appointment of bookrunners can advance preparation, but it does not establish the final offer size, pricing or admission date.

Dangote Cement Plc produces and sells cement across Sub-Saharan Africa, with operations in ten countries and production capacity of 55.0 million tonnes per year, according to the company website. Its strategy focuses on serving construction demand in West and Central Africa and using Nigeria as an export hub. The group competes with regional cement producers including BUA Cement and Lafarge Africa in Nigeria, while its broad African footprint gives it a larger geographic reach than more locally focused rivals.
Broader market conditions remain relevant for companies seeking international listings. Current market reports provide the wider market context.

JBL Stock Jumps 6% After UBS Upgrade — How Amazon, Meta, Google Could Power Jabil’s AI Growth
sum: Shares of Jabil Inc. (JBL) jumped nearly 6% on Tuesday after UBS upgraded the stock to ‘Buy’ from ‘Neutral,’ as the firm sees Big Tech’s AI investments providing a boost to the company in the coming years.
By midday Tuesday, JBL stock had pared some of its gains but was still trading 4.3% higher.
UBS analyst David Vogt upgraded Jabil to ‘Buy’ while keeping the price target unchanged at $430, implying nearly 28% upside from Monday’s close.

The firm said “product road maps” from key customers, including Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN), Meta Platforms Inc. (META), and Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL), could mean potentially faster growth than previously expected.

“We upgrade Jabil to Buy on a multi-year growth cycle fueled by AI investment from Amazon, Meta, and Google,” the analyst wrote, according to a report in Barron’s. UBS added that rising health care demand and “scaling automation and robotics markets” will also be tailwinds for the company.
The firm forecasts Jabil’s AI-related revenue growing by about 50% to $20.3 billion in fiscal 2027, up from $13.5 billion in fiscal 2026.

Amazon is the key for Jabil, according to UBS, the Barron’s report stated. “Amazon, Jabil’s largest AI partner, plans to accelerate deployment of its Graviton CPUs and Trainium AI ASICs over the next several years,” the analyst wrote.

items.t: UBS Flags a Bullish Setup in Tesla Stock and Lifts Its Price Target
sum: UBS just raised its Tesla price target and called the risk/reward tactically favorable, but the same stock lost 32% in 30 days after one bad earnings report. Here is what the bull case actually rests on.

UBS analyst Joseph Spak raised his price target on Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA | TSLA Price Prediction) to $391, according to UBS from $385, according to UBS and kept his Buy rating. The argument behind the modest bump carries the weight. Tesla shares trade at $378.02, down 16.6% over the past year and 15.94% year to date. They are also up 7.14% over the past week and 6.76% over the past month. Spak is making a tactical call on a stock that has started moving again after a weak year.

Spak’s core claim is direct: “Tesla remains more sentiment- than results-driven, and at current levels, the risk/reward looks tactically favorable.” Put simply, the share price moves on what investors expect from robotaxis, robots and AI. Quarterly profits play a smaller role.

The record supports him. In Q2 2026, Tesla earned $0.33 per share, missing the $0.5367 estimate. The stock fell 14.52% on the day of the report, then gained 9.15% over the next 30 days. The S&P 500 ETF rose 3.43% over the same period. At roughly 396x earnings, the price rests on expectations about the future: Robotaxi service in seven U.S. metros and 1.48M active FSD subscriptions. Investors who value Tesla on fundamentals will find current profits explain little of the stock’s behavior.

The call is about near-term positioning. Spak’s move from $385 to $391 tells you the underlying model barely changed. Spak’s message is that conditions currently favor the bulls. Third-quarter deliveries came in ahead of consensus estimates, and options traders lean bullish, with a full-chain put/call ratio of 0.59. That means call contracts outnumber puts.

A stock that rises on mood can fall on mood too, even when the business hasn’t changed. Today Tesla is down 0.7% in premarket trading after European self-driving approvals were delayed. After the Q4 2024 report, shares lost 32.04% over 30 days.

The fundamentals give little support if the mood turns. Operating margin fell to 1.4% in Q2. Free cash flow came in at -$1.09B, and management expects 2026 capex above $25 billion. Automotive margins excluding credits slipped from 19.2% to 16.3%.

IG Group sell-off is an overreaction, says UBS
sum: IG Group Holdings Plc (LSE:IGG), the online trading platform, suffered a 22% share-price fall last Friday (Oct. 2) after cutting its 2026 revenue and EBITDA guidance, but UBS described the sell-off as an overreaction.
The bank's analyst Haley Tam and colleagues cut their earnings-per-share forecasts by 13% for 2026 through 2028 and reduced the price target to 1,425p from 1,700p, while retaining a 'buy' rating.

UBS said IG's weaker third-quarter performance reflected lower over-the-counter, or OTC, revenue retention, which fell to about 70% from an average of about 80% since market-making optimisation measures were introduced in the second half of 2025.
The broker said those measures had improved average retention from about 75% historically to 80% but created greater short-term volatility that contributed to the latest decline.
IG now expects 2026 revenue growth in the mid-single-digit percentage range and an EBITDA margin in the low 40s, below the stronger outlook issued earlier this year.

UBS said the bigger issue for investors was not simply the earnings miss but the damage to confidence after IG cut guidance only four months after raising it, following the cancellation of buybacks and a larger-than-expected acquisition.

The broker believes the market has treated the Q3 weakness as a permanent deterioration when it is more likely to be a one-off setback, although it now forecasts only 7% organic revenue growth annually between 2025 and 2030.

Boeing stock rises on $20B US Navy contract; UBS says selloff gone too far
sum: Buy Boeing (BA). The $20B+ F/A-XX award removes a major overhang on defense participation and supports a longer-duration backlog, while UBS argues the selloff already priced in near-term cash-flow hits (MAX 10 software delay, timeline setbacks). With normalized free cash flow still intact in UBS’s view, the stock’s risk/reward improves as certification uncertainty clears and investors refocus on commercial cash generation.
Key Risk: A prolonged 737 MAX 10 software/certification problem that pushes deliveries and cash flow out by months, forcing further balance-sheet stress.

Sell Northrop Grumman (NOC). The F/A-XX award to Boeing effectively sidelines NOC from the next-generation fighter program for the foreseeable future, and the market already reacted with a premarket drop. With less upside from this specific program, NOC’s defense growth narrative weakens versus peers that still have credible fighter participation.
Key Risk: NOC wins other major near-term defense programs that offset the lost F/A-XX opportunity and restore earnings momentum.
- The award is Boeing’s second sixth-generation fighter win in a year.
- Defense win significant, but Boeing’s commercial production, cash flow are key.

Meesho shares jump 12% as UBS sees up to 19% upside
sum: Meesho shares jumped up to 12 percent in Tuesday's trading session after brokerage firm UBS raised its target price on the stock, marking the biggest single-day gain in the last three months.

UBS maintained its "buy" recommendation on Meesho and raised its target price to Rs 260 per share from Rs 210. The revised target indicates an upside potential of 18.6 percent from the previous closing price.

"We value Meesho using a combination of DCF and multiples. On the multiples approach, we apply a 40x EV/EBITDA multiple (unchanged) on 3YF EBITDA, i.e. average of FY30-31, and discount it back by two years, deriving a PT of Rs 260," UBS said.

While its FY27 estimates are largely unchanged, UBS raised its FY29-31 NMV estimates by 7-18 percent, with a similar increase in contribution profit estimates and a 20-40 percent increase in EBITDA estimates.

"Higher NMV forecasts reflect the continued flywheel from sellers (+81 percent YoY to 1.04 million in Q1FY27), buyers (+29 percent YoY to 274 million), coupled with rapid expansion in SKUs and logistics partners," it said.
The brokerage said the larger increase in EBITDA estimates reflects a stronger medium-term margin trajectory, driven by improving ads monetisation and logistics economics.

Management remains confident in the FY27 growth outlook. Although the shift in Diwali from October 2025 to November 2026 should result in slower growth in Q2 and faster growth in Q3, low-30s NMV growth remains achievable for FY27, UBS said.

Kalyan Jewellers stock rises as UBS initiates coverage with Buy, sees 50% upside
sum: Kalyan Jewellers India shares rose in early trade on Tuesday after UBS initiated coverage on the jewellery retailer with a ‘buy’ rating and a target price of Rs 900 per share, implying an upside of nearly 50 percent from Friday’s closing price. The Kalyan Jewellers stock was trading 1.5 percent higher at Rs 610 in early deals. The shares had closed 1.89 percent lower at Rs 601.15 on Friday. Indian stock markets were shut on Monday for a holiday.

UBS said Kalyan Jewellers has emerged as a pan-India jewellery retailer, replicating market leader Titan’s footprint while building a strong hyper-local value proposition. The brokerage highlighted the company’s capital-light franchise-owned, company-operated (FOCO) model, which is now well established and allows Kalyan Jewellers to expand its network aggressively. Its pace of store additions is nearly twice that of Titan, according to UBS.

Kalyan Jewellers’ revenue grew at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of around 35 percent between FY22 and FY26, among the highest growth rates in the organised jewellery industry, UBS said. The brokerage expects the company’s revenue and earnings to compound at around 23 percent annually over the next five years, supported by continued network expansion.

UBS also sees scope for a further re-rating in the stock despite its six-fold appreciation between FY22 and FY26. Kalyan Jewellers trades at around 30 times estimated FY28 earnings, representing a roughly 45 percent discount to Titan, according to the brokerage.

Kalyan Jewellers shares have gained more than 24 percent so far in 2026, significantly outperforming the Nifty 50, which has declined around 10.5 percent over the same period. The company had a market capitalisation of around Rs 62,100 crore at Friday’s close.
The broader market was also higher on Tuesday. At 9:25 am, the Sensex was up 266 points, or 0.36 percent, at 75,047.91, while the Nifty 50 gained 69 points, or 0.29 percent, to 23,466.80.

sum: General Dynamics Corporation stock (ISIN US3695501086) closed at USD 355.90 on the NYSE on September 11, 2026, representing a 0.47 percent gain versus the prior close as per recent market data. According to Yahoo Finance on September 14, 2026, UBS recently raised its price target on General Dynamics stock from USD 395 to USD 408 while maintaining a Neutral rating, giving investors a fresh reference point for valuation.

As of September 14, 2026, General Dynamics stock sits in an environment of broadly constructive analyst coverage, with an average price target of USD 422.30 and a high target of USD 465 according to Yahoo Finance. In the same overview, the lowest documented target stands at USD 319, illustrating a spread of roughly USD 146 between the most cautious and most optimistic views, which underscores the debate around how far the current defense cycle can carry earnings and cash flow.

UBS's move on September 8, 2026 to lift its General Dynamics price target from USD 395 to USD 408 while keeping the rating at Neutral, as reported by Yahoo Finance, adds nuance to the picture: the bank acknowledges some upside from current levels but stops short of a full Buy recommendation. For investors, that combination of a modest target increase and a middle-of-the-road rating can signal a view that most of the easy gains from recent program wins and backlog expansion may already be reflected in the share price.

General Dynamics stock ended trading at USD 355.90 on September 11, 2026 on the NYSE, up 1.65 dollars or 0.47 percent on the day, as outlined by Yahoo Finance. That closing level is close to the current average analyst target of USD 422.30, leaving a gap of about USD 66.40 or roughly 18.7 percent between the market price and the consensus view, which many investors will interpret as a potential upside corridor if the company delivers on its growth and margin ambitions.

sum: - Price change for Bloom Energy stock in the last 6 months: -79%

UBS reiterated its buy rating on Bloom Energy (BE) stock this week, even as shares have pulled back more than 20% since late June.

The concern weighing on Bloom Energy stock centers on raw materials, specifically the risk that scandium, a rare element used in Bloom’s fuel cell technology, could become a bottleneck for the company’s growth.

UBS analyst Manav Gupta directly pushed back on that concern. In a Thursday note to clients, he said the recent pullback actually creates an attractive buying opportunity, arguing that fears around raw material sourcing, and scandium specifically, are overstated.

Gupta pointed out that Bloom has developed its own proprietary process to secure the scandium it needs, which helps insulate the company from broader supply constraints that might affect competitors relying on more traditional sourcing methods.
Based on this view, UBS kept its 12-month price target at $350, which implies about 36% upside from Thursday’s closing price.
